Solution 3 is correct: the maximum is $2^{999}-2^{499}$.

**Upper bound.** Since $A\cap(S\setminus A)=\emptyset$, $P$ contains at most one set from each of the $2^{999}$ complementary pairs $\{A,S\setminus A\}$. If $A'=S\setminus A$ (equivalently, $A$ contains exactly one element of each reflection pair $\{i,1001-i\}$), then $A\in P$ forces $A'=S\setminus A\in P$, which violates condition 2. These "transversals" number $2^{500}$ and form $2^{499}$ complementary pairs, both of whose members are excluded. So $|P|\le 2^{999}-2^{499}$.

**Construction.**
- Take all subsets of size $\ge 501$. Any two intersect because their sizes sum to more than 1000, and the family is reflection-closed because reflection preserves size. There are $\frac{2^{1000}-\binom{1000}{500}}{2}$ of them.
- Among the non-transversal 500-element sets, group them into reflection-and-complement orbits $\{A,A',S\setminus A,S\setminus A'\}$ (or smaller when $A'=A$). From each orbit, take $\{A,A'\}$, or $\{A\}$ if $A'=A$. This choice is reflection-closed, contains no complementary pair (so it is intersecting), and meets $\{A,S\setminus A\}$ in exactly one set. It gives $\frac{\binom{1000}{500}-2^{500}}{2}$ sets.
- A 500-set and a set of size $\ge 501$ always intersect, since $500+501>1000$.

The total is $\frac{2^{1000}-2^{500}}{2}=2^{999}-2^{499}$, matching the bound.

**Checking the others.**
- Solution 1 gives $\frac{2^{1000}-\binom{1000}{500}}{2}+\binom{998}{498}$. Since $\binom{1000}{500}/2$ is roughly $2^{993}$, this is far below $2^{999}-2^{499}$, so it is not the maximum.
- Solution 2 gives $2^{999}$, which exceeds the proven upper bound $2^{999}-2^{499}$, so it is impossible.

**Decimal check of Solution 3.** The decimal string for Solution 3 ends in 0000. Working modulo 10000, $2^{999}\equiv 2^{499}\equiv 4688$, so $2^{999}-2^{499}\equiv 0$, consistent with that ending.

CHOICE: 3
